fix: Interning leaks one Box and grows a Vec that is linearly scanned on every call, keyed by exact float values. Callers that build Interval/Split/Flipped curves from changing parameters inside a frame loop (e.g. a changing `begin`) leak a new allocation and make each later lookup slower, so memory and per-frame cost grow without bound. Either (a) do not intern: make Curve::Flipped hold an owned/boxed-free representation (e.g. flatten into a recursive enum with fixed-size payload, or store the inner curve by value via a small fixed array), or (b) if `&'static` is required, document that flipping non-cubic composite curves is intended for static curve constants only and add a `try_flipped`/`maybe_flipped` that returns Option/Result for dynamic parameters. Keep the existing behavior for constant curves. Consider the same change for catmull_rom (line 311).
